name: Global food prices
summary: FAO food price index 133.9 in October, below the 135 Alert line but up 5.9% on a year; next release 4 Dec
state: The FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.9 points in October, down 1.2% on September but 5.9% above October 2025 (FAO; Food Ingredients First). Sugar rose 6.6% for a fourth monthly rise while cereals fell 4.5%. The annual rise meets the Watch line and the index stays below 135; searches on 20 Nov found no staple export bans by several major exporters, and the next release is due on 4 Dec.
for_you: Global food costs are higher than a year ago, which tends to feed into supermarket prices with a lag and hits import-dependent countries hardest.
rubric_hit: FFPI 133.9 in 120–135 Watch band and +5.9% y/y > +5%

sources.title: Food Ingredients First — FAO Food Price Index falls in October as sugar prices continue to climb

why: Food prices drive inflation, hunger and political unrest; poorer countries spend up to half of income on food.
drivers: Harvests, weather, fertiliser and energy costs, export bans, conflict in breadbaskets.

rubric.alert: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.
rubric.watch: FFPI 120–135, or y/y > +5%, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: FAO Food Price Index < 120 and y/y change < +5%.
